title: St Albans
intro: A Roman city and medieval market town, with a great abbey cathedral, a Roman theatre and a lakeside park over the old city walls.

items.name: St Albans Cathedral
items.blurb: The abbey church on the site of Alban's martyrdom, with a Norman tower built partly of Roman bricks and one of the longest naves in England.
items.tip: Free to enter; the Saturday market is a short walk away.

items.name: Verulamium Park
items.blurb: A big lakeside park below the cathedral on the site of the Roman city, with stretches of Roman wall and a hypocaust to see.
items.tip: Walk up from the lake to the cathedral for the classic view.

items.name: Roman Theatre of Verulamium
items.blurb: The only visible Roman theatre in Britain, built around 140 AD, in fields beside the Gorhambury estate.
items.tip: Combine it with the Verulamium Museum across the road.

items.name: Clock Tower
items.blurb: A medieval belfry built in the early 1400s, the only surviving town belfry of its kind in England, with views from the top.
items.tip: Open to climb at weekends in summer.

items.name: Fishpool Street
items.blurb: A winding old street of timber-framed and Georgian houses running down from the cathedral to St Michael's and the river.
items.tip: Finish at Ye Olde Fighting Cocks by the lake.

items.name: St Albans Market
items.blurb: A street market held on Wednesdays and Saturdays along St Peter's Street, a tradition going back to the Middle Ages.
